name: Girru 1.4.1
body:
## Girru 1.4.1

- Refresh desktop setup with an animated discovery view, readable file labels, responsive layouts and improved team editing.
- Discover accessible projects, memory, skills, MCP connections and SSH identity metadata before creating the team.
- Improve durable background memory imports, workspace reuse and discovery responsiveness.
- Handle temporary Windows file locks when saving discovery progress and wait for filesystem workers to finish during shutdown.
- Preserve existing accounts, workspaces and local sessions when updating.

### Downloads
Choose the installer matching your operating system and CPU. SHA256SUMS manifests accompany the downloads.

macOS builds are ad-hoc signed and are not notarized. Windows builds are unsigned. First-open instructions are in the README.

Built from main commit `9058e1aacbd25583ddced88979e559c2b466998e`.

name: Girru 1.4.0
body:
Girru 1.4.0 is the first release under the Girru name. Dpro stays the company behind it. Workspaces from Dpro 1.3.2 update in place and keep their accounts, conversations and encrypted credentials.

## First run
- Setup is one window, one question per screen: your account, then your AI tools, then a free local model, then your team.
- **AI tools.** Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI show whether they are installed and signed in. Install and Sign in run right away in Girru's terminal.
- **Local model.** Girru checks what is already in Ollama and offers it first. A new download is sized below your computer's memory.
- **Team.** Choose 3 to 500 agents, or type a number up to 1000. Answer "What is your work?" if you like, and pick from 16 departments. Then see how the agents are split, and hire them all at once. Your first chat opens with the Main agent.

## Chat
- **Window.** A chat window with a chats-only sidebar, projects with folders, a side panel and a terminal under the chat.
- **Composer.** Mode, Thinking level and model choice in the composer.
- **Live work.** Replies come in live. Approvals show inside the chat, and you can steer or undo a run.
- **Coding apps.** Claude Code, Codex and Gemini work as members of the team: hand-off cards, images, thinking level, and a Stop button.
- **Results.** Pull request state and changed files show on a chat's Results card.

## Agents
- **Organisation.** An org chart with sub-agents, and agent files.
- **Personality and specialties.** Each agent's personality, plus a library of professional specialties with reviewed content updates.
- **Rules.** Agents › Rules holds your rules for how agents work, with cases and a disagreement check.

## Tasks
- Open a task as its own page.
- One task file per project.
- Repeating tasks, a task side bar and a Scheduled filter.

## Store and apps
- **The Store** is its own section. My apps sits inside it, and private apps can be added from a folder.
- **Apps moved to the Store:** SEO, WAF Security and Server Monitor.
- **Chat channels** all run through Agent Connect.

## Desktop
- **Mac app.** Rounded macOS icon, app updates, and extensions next to the program.
- **Backups.** Automatic backup is in Settings › Backups.

## Safety
- **Dependencies.** Updated backend and desktop build dependencies; locked dependency audits report no known vulnerabilities.
- **Trading connection.** The Alpaca connection uses a built-in client with authenticated requests, bounded request timeouts and redirect refusal.
- **Isolation.** Agent code runs in an isolated process.
- **Reply sources.** A subscription reply source is never imported from a shared settings file.
- **Settings.** MCP connections stay inside Settings.

macOS builds are ad-hoc signed and not notarized; Windows builds are unsigned. Each platform comes with a SHA256 checksum file.

name: Dpro 1.3.2
body:
Dpro 1.3.2 packages the current Electron desktop application for macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Windows x64 and Linux x64.

- Reuse existing accounts, conversations, encrypted credentials and the selected workspace during updates.
- Resume background imports after restart, preserve progress and avoid duplicate imports.
- Include current account, team, settings and import improvements.
- Harden secret redaction, diagnostic records, process arguments and private file access; update vulnerable runtime dependencies.

The legacy desktop publishing pipelines are retired. These installers are built from the same main revision and include platform SHA256 manifests. macOS builds are unsigned and not notarized.

Validation: platform UI, desktop and backend persistence/security tests; dependency audits; full-history secret scan; CodeQL review; and an isolated old-to-new macOS update and restart using fictional accounts, conversations and encrypted credentials.
